chunk_findings.detail: The new assertion `h.move(h.path("self"), h.path("self"))` treats moving a directory onto itself as a no-op. For the real disk adapter, `_Disk.move` delegates to `shutil.move`; on CPython, `shutil.move('/.../self', '/.../self')` does not return for an existing directory: `_destinsrc` considers the destination to be inside the source and raises `shutil.Error("Cannot move a directory '...' into itself '...'.")`. This shared conformance test therefore fails before reaching the `copy_tree` parity check.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_adapter_fs.py:90 (the shared conformance move-into-itself case)

chunk_findings.detail: Same-path-prefix copies are no longer refused and are defined as one flat pass over the original tree, which is not what `shutil.copytree` does. `copytree` snapshots each directory with `os.scandir` and recurses after sibling copies, so a file written into the destination (which still lies under the source) is copied again. Given `self/one.txt` and `self/sub/two.txt`, `copy_tree("self", "self/sub", dirs_exist_ok=True)`, and a listing order of `one.txt` then `sub` (typical after creating those two entries in that order), LocalFs also writes `self/sub/sub/one.txt`. A one-pass map of the original files never does. The new shared assertions only read `self/sub/one.txt` and `self/sub/sub/two.txt`, which both orders and both adapters produce, so the nested case this change claims to lock down still passes while the trees differ.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fakes/fs.py:128

chunk_findings.detail: `f.copy_tree("/z", "/z/sub", dirs_exist_ok=True)` is followed only by checks that `/z/sub/f` and `/z/sub/empty` still exist. Those paths are the pre-copy tree; a no-op (the old `ValueError` path, or a loop that copies nothing) satisfies the assert. It does not require `/z/sub/sub/f`, so this case does not hold the fake to the snapshot copy the comment describes.

chunk_findings.detail: `if self._under(s):` is used for `src == dst` with `dirs_exist_ok=True` to detect a file that would copy onto itself, but `_under` also contains directory entries. The new test at tests/test_adapter_fs.py:285 builds exactly that directory-only case: `/z` contains the empty child `/z/empty`, and the test expects `e2.copy_tree("/z", "/z", dirs_exist_ok=True)` to return. Since `_under('/z')` includes `/z/empty`, the function raises `Error` instead, so the test itself fails. The comment claims a directory-only tree falls through as a no-op, but that is only true when `_under` is empty, not when it contains empty directories.

evidence.note: Probed each of the 5 homes: digest/proc/resources are wholly adapter-shaped (stdlib-only); fsio splits into the Fsio port (tempfile/fcntl) vs the Managed doc-region stamping (core.events.is_older + FORMAT_LEVEL/__version__); git inverts core.outcome.FAIL (exit=1 by value); tomlcfg.read overlay is config-coupled via config_sections._layers.read_toml/ConfigConflict. Empirically confirmed the shim/monkeypatch seams and 20KB splits.

r-adapters (one implementation per function), r-small-files (<20KB: proc 8.4K+19.4K, fsio 15.8K+15.3K, git 19.9K), D-adapters-answers (adapters imports no higher layer; baselines only shrink: subprocess-home/fsio-home/digest-home homes moved, never added), tests-first no behaviour change (340+ tests green).

5 commits moved digest/resources/proc(+proc_server)/fsio/git into ddflow.adapters behind shims; contracts+baselines+archdeps+test_arch_deps repointed. tomlcfg deliberately NOT moved: its overlay loader reads config files with merge-conflict detection (ConfigConflict) + layer paths = a config concern, not a tomllib/tomlkit adapter.

data.alternatives: Rejected: (a) move only the text-edit and drop overlay_table from the Toml port — a port API change rippling to fakes/conformance/callers, needs the coordinator; (b) move tomlcfg whole — would import config_sections._layers from adapters, a layers-contract violation.
data.consequences: tomlkit-home and the Toml port stay in infra/config for now; a follow-up can move only upsert/remove/move_keys into ddflow.adapters.tomlcfg and shrink the Toml port to the text-edit methods.
data.context: The task node 'move infra.tomlcfg into ddflow.adapters' treats tomlcfg as a single adapter family, but tomlcfg is mixed: its Toml port declares both the overlay loader and the comment-preserving write-back. The overlay loader is config-file reading.
data.decision: ADP-migrate-homes migrates 4 of its 5 named homes into ddflow/adapters (proc, git, fsio, digest) plus the resources dependency; ddflow.infra.tomlcfg stays where it is. Only the pure TOML text-edit (upsert/remove/move_keys + value/basic_string/literal) is a tomllib/tomlkit adapter; overlay_table/overlay_array/skipped_fields/config_paths/locked read config files through config_sections._layers.read_toml (merge-conflict detection raising ConfigConflict) and layer_path/LAYERS, which is a config-layer concern, so moving tomlcfg wholesale would drag config concerns into the bottom adapters layer and force a redesign of the Toml port (dropping its config-overlay method).

chunk_findings.detail: `of_obj` throws away `size` for every algorithm except exactly `"blake2b"`, even though the doc says `size` is blake2's `digest_size` and `hashlib` accepts it for both `blake2b` and `blake2s`. Given `of_obj({"x": 1}, algo="blake2s", size=8)`, it returns the default 32-byte blake2s digest (64 hex chars) instead of a 8-byte digest (16 hex chars). The guard should allow both blake2 variants, e.g. `algo in ("blake2b", "blake2s")`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/digest.py:of_obj

chunk_findings.detail: The optional `\]?` lets the regex match unclosed tokens such as `[REDACTED` or `[REDACTED:secret`, even though the documented marker spellings are the closed `[REDACTED]` and `[REDACTED:<kind>]`. For example, `normalize_markers("literal [REDACTED text")` returns `"literal [REDACTED] text"`, so a non-marker prefix is rewritten. With `normalize_text`, two different strings like `"literal [REDACTED text"` and `"literal [REDACTED] text"` both normalize to the same value, causing false deduplication if these digests are used for duplicate checks.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/digest.py:MARKER

chunk_findings.detail: `normalized` returns a `list` for any tuple input: `normalized(("a [REDACTED:x]",))` evaluates to `["a [REDACTED]"]`. This contradicts the function's own contract that an object's "shape and every other value are unchanged" and changes the Python type, which can alter downstream equality or type-sensitive handling. It should preserve tuples.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/digest.py:normalized

chunk_findings.detail: `parse_status` stores rename/copy fields backwards: `git status --porcelain -z` emits the original path first and the destination path second (for `git mv old new`, the records are `R  old\0new\0`). This code puts the first record into `StatusEntry.path` and the second into `StatusEntry.orig`, so `StatusEntry.line()` produces `R  new -> old`, and callers that use `StatusEntry.path` get the pre-rename path rather than the current work-tree path.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/git.py:parse_status

chunk_findings.detail: `read_blobs` assumes every `git cat-file --batch` response is `<sha> <type> <size>`, but for a missing object git prints `<sha> missing` and still exits successfully. Given `shas=["<missing-object-sha>"]`, `check=True` does not raise, and `sha, _kind, size = data[i:nl].decode().split()` receives two fields and raises `ValueError`, not the documented `GitError`; this breaks callers in a partial clone or corrupt object store.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/git.py:read_blobs

chunk_findings.detail: `capture(["echo", "hi"], timeout=10, encoding="utf-8")` passes both `text=True` and a non-`None` `encoding` (and the same applies to `errors`) to `subprocess.run`. CPython's `subprocess.Popen` rejects `text` combined with `encoding`/`errors` by raising `ValueError`, but `capture` only catches `TimeoutExpired`, `SubprocessError`, and `OSError`. The signature explicitly exposes `encoding` and `errors`, so any caller exercising those documented parameters gets an unhandled `ValueError` instead of a `Captured` value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/proc.py:capture

chunk_findings.detail: The old top-level imports above the moved block, such as `import fcntl` and `import secrets`, no longer have any remaining references in this file because their only uses were in the removed `file_lock` and `_temp_beside` bodies now moved to `ddflow/adapters/fsio.py`. Since the project’s flake8 run enforces F401 (the new wildcard import line is explicitly `# noqa: F401,F403`), running the linter on `ddflow/infra/fsio.py` will fail with F401 for these now-unused imports, breaking CI despite the runtime behavior of the shim being unaffected.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/fsio.py:top imports

chunk_findings.detail: The old tuple included `ddflow.infra.git`; this change moves `ddflow/infra/git.py`'s implementation into `ddflow/adapters/git.py` (per the manifest, `ddflow/infra/git.py` loses 480 lines and `ddflow/adapters/git.py` gains 482), so the direct `subprocess` import that justified the old entry now lives at `ddflow.adapters.git`. The new tuple lists only `ddflow.adapters.proc` and `ddflow.adapters.proc_server`, and no `ddflow.adapters.git` allowlist was added under `importlinter-subprocess-home`. Running the architecture import contract tests will flag `ddflow.adapters.git -> subprocess` as illegal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:52 STDLIB_HOMES["subprocess"]

chunk_findings.detail: The fsio implementation moved from `ddflow.infra.fsio` to `ddflow.adapters.fsio`—the adjacent `fsio` entry was updated accordingly—but the `shutil` home still points at `ddflow.infra.fsio`. The re-export shim at `ddflow.infra.fsio` no longer contains the `shutil` import; the real importer is now `ddflow.adapters.fsio`. The `shutil-home` architecture contract is therefore bound to the shim rather than the module that actually imports `shutil`, so the guard either misses the real importer or flags `ddflow.adapters.fsio -> shutil`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:54 STDLIB_HOMES["shutil"]

chunk_findings.detail: The stated migration includes moving `infra.tomlcfg` into `ddflow.adapters` and updating every contract's home entry in the same change, but this assertion still requires `reports["tomlkit"].home == ("ddflow.infra.tomlcfg",)` and the manifest contains no `ddflow/adapters/tomlcfg.py`. chunk_findings.detail: `replace_text` only forces an in-place write when `st_nlink > 1`, the owner differs, or `os.access(..., W_OK)` is false. A user-owned writable FIFO (nlink 1) therefore takes `atomic_write` and `os.replace`, which unlinks the pipe and leaves a regular file. `Path.write_text` would open the FIFO and write into it, keeping the inode. The same check is false for an empty directory on filesystems that report directory nlink 1 (btrfs): `os.replace` deletes the directory and installs a file, while `write_text` raises `IsADirectoryError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/fsio.py:replace_text

chunk_findings.detail: `git -C` makes every relative path repo-relative, but these helpers pass the caller's path unchanged. `bundle_heads(Path("out/repo.bundle"))` runs `git -C out bundle list-heads out/repo.bundle`, which looks for `out/out/repo.bundle` and raises `GitError` even though the file exists. `bundle_create(repo, Path("bundles/x.bundle"), ref)` and `fetch_untrusted(repo, Path("incoming.bundle"), ...)` likewise write or fetch `repo / relative` instead of the path relative to the process cwd; a relative source that also exists inside the repo fetches that other file.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/git.py:bundle_heads

chunk_findings.detail: `git cat-file --batch` exits 0 and prints `<object> missing` when a sha is absent, so `check=True` does not raise. Given `shas=["deadbeef"]` not in the repo, `sha, _kind, size = data[i:nl].decode().split()` raises `ValueError` instead of `GitError`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/git.py:read_blobs

chunk_findings.detail: `child.wait(timeout=grace_s)` raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, but the handler catches the bare name `TimeoutExpired`, which is never imported. When the child is still alive after `grace_s`, that path raises `NameError` instead of `stop_group` plus `os._exit(0)`, so the session is not ended and the documented exit-0 contract is missed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/proc_server.py:relay_stdio

chunk_findings.detail: Re-exporting `_shell_group` (and the other underscored seams) onto this module does not preserve the patch point the comment claims. `run_shell` is the function object defined in `ddflow.adapters.proc_server`; its call to `_shell_group` is resolved in that module’s globals. `patch("ddflow.infra.proc._shell_group", ...)` then `ddflow.infra.proc.run_shell("true", timeout_s=1)` still runs the real `_shell_group`, so the compatibility shim does not keep the old monkeypatch contract. The same applies to `_feed_stdin`, `_drain`, `_start_watcher`, and `_arm_watcher`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/proc.py

chunk_findings.detail: `STDLIB_HOMES["shutil"]` still names `ddflow.infra.fsio` after this move, while `"fsio"` was updated to `ddflow.adapters.fsio`. The infra module is now a re-export shim (implementation removed; manifest shows +9/−352), so it no longer imports `shutil`. The code that does lives in `ddflow.adapters.fsio`. The home contract therefore authorizes a module that does not perform the import and forbids the one that does: an import-linter/archdeps check of `import shutil` inside the moved fsio implementation fails, and the stated “update every contract's home entry” step was missed for this family.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:53

chunk_findings.detail: `normalized` handles tuples by returning a list (`return [normalized(v) for v in obj]`), but its own docstring says the object's “shape and every other value are unchanged.” Given input `normalized((1, "[REDACTED]"))`, the result is `[1, "[REDACTED]"]` — a list, not a tuple. This changes the Python container type for tuple inputs, so any caller that relies on the returned object being tuple-like (for example, for equality or hashing before a later digest/comparison step) gets wrong behavior even though only marker normalization was requested.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/digest.py:normalized

chunk_findings.detail: `replace_process` is implemented as `os.execve(path, argv, env)`, but `os.execve` does not exist in CPython on Windows. The same process layer explicitly targets Windows (`TIMEOUTS["instant"]` covers “a `taskkill`”), so a Windows execution of this function — e.g. `replace_process(r"C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe", ["cmd"], dict(os.environ))` — raises `AttributeError: module 'os' has no attribute 'execve'` instead of replacing the process, contradicting the doc’s “Returns only by raising `OSError`.”
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/proc.py:replace_process

chunk_findings.detail: `relay_stdio` uses `except TimeoutExpired:` but `TimeoutExpired` is never imported or qualified; the file only has `import subprocess`. When the relayed child does not exit within `grace_s`, `child.wait(timeout=grace_s)` raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, and evaluating the undefined name in the `except` clause then raises `NameError`. The intended `stop_group(child); code = 0` never runs, so an over-grace child is left running instead of being killed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/proc_server.py:relay_stdio

chunk_findings.detail: The shim re-exports `_shell_group` as an alias, but `ddflow.infra.proc.run_shell` is now the `ddflow.adapters.proc_server.run_shell` function object. Its internal `_shell_group` lookup resolves in `ddflow.adapters.proc_server.__globals__`, not in this shim module. Given `unittest.mock.patch("ddflow.infra.proc._shell_group", fake)` followed by `ddflow.infra.proc.run_shell(...)`, the patched `fake` is never called; the real `_shell_group` executes the command. The docstring promises this seam is re-exported exactly because proc tests patch it, so the compatibility re-export does not provide the old patching behavior.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/proc.py:15

chunk_findings.detail: The change’s own intent (D-adapters-answers) says `ddflow.infra.tomlcfg` moves into `ddflow.adapters.tomlcfg` and every contract’s home entry is updated in this same change. The test still asserts `reports["tomlkit"].home == ("ddflow.infra.tomlcfg",)`, and the manifest contains no `ddflow/adapters/tomlcfg.py` or `ddflow/infra/tomlcfg.py` change. So either the `.importlinter`/contract migration for `tomlkit` was not done, or this assertion now pins the old wrong home and would fail once the contract is updated. Both cases violate the stated move for `tomlcfg`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_arch_deps.py:test_violations_are_importers_outside_the_home

chunk_findings.detail: `of_obj` forwards `size` only when `algo == "blake2b"`. `blake2s` also takes `digest_size`. Given `of_obj({"a": 1}, "blake2s", size=8)`, the call becomes `content_digest(..., size=None)` and returns a 64-character digest instead of the 16-character digest of an 8-byte blake2s hash. The docstring says `size` is blake2's `digest_size` and is dropped only for algorithms that have no such setting, so this input is wrong, not a documented limitation.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/digest.py:of_obj

chunk_findings.detail: `normalized` documents that shape is unchanged, but `isinstance(obj, (list, tuple))` always returns a list. Given `("keep",)`, the result is `["keep"]`. A caller that preserves tuple vs list (or checks `isinstance(..., tuple)` after normalization) sees a different value than the one described.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/digest.py:normalized

chunk_findings.detail: `read_blobs` documents that it raises `GitError`, but a missing or non-blob id makes `cat-file --batch` exit 0 and print `<sha> missing` (two fields, no size). `sha, _kind, size = data[i:nl].decode().split()` then raises `ValueError`, and a truncated batch with no newline raises `ValueError` from `data.index`. Callers that only catch `GitError` (the contract used by `tree_entries` / `commit_tree`) do not see a git failure. Input: `read_blobs(repo, ["deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef"])` when that object is absent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/git.py:read_blobs

chunk_findings.detail: `run` always invokes `git -C <repo>`, so every relative path in argv is resolved from that directory, not the process cwd. `bundle_heads(Path("artifacts/demo.bundle"))` becomes `git -C artifacts bundle list-heads artifacts/demo.bundle`, which opens `artifacts/artifacts/demo.bundle` and raises `GitError` even though `artifacts/demo.bundle` exists. The same `-C` shift mis-places a relative `dest` in `bundle_create` and a relative `source` in `fetch_untrusted` (written or read under the repo, not the path the caller passed). Absolute paths hide it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/git.py:bundle_heads

chunk_findings.detail: `relay_stdio` catches bare `TimeoutExpired`, which is never imported (only `subprocess` is). `Popen.wait(timeout=grace_s)` raises `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`. Given a child that stays alive past `grace_s`, the handler raises `NameError` instead of `stop_group` and `os._exit(0)`, so the grace path the docstring specifies never runs and this process does not take the child's exit.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/proc_server.py:130

chunk_findings.detail: `run_piped` arms `threading.Timer(timeout, kill_group, (p,))` with no reap check, while `kill_group` documents that `os.killpg(p.pid, SIGKILL)` is only safe before the pid is reaped. If `work` calls `p.wait()`/`poll()` and reaps the child as the timer fires (timeout elapses in that window, before `finally` `clock.cancel()`), `kill_group` signals that pid after it can be recycled, which can SIGKILL an unrelated process. The timer callback does not consult `p.poll()`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/adapters/proc_server.py:75

chunk_findings.detail: Re-exporting `_shell_group` (and `_feed_stdin`, `_drain`, `_start_watcher`, `_arm_watcher`) does not preserve the patch seam the docstring claims. `run_shell` lives in `ddflow.adapters.proc_server` and resolves `_shell_group` in that module’s globals. `patch("ddflow.infra.proc._shell_group", fake)` only rebinds the name in this shim, so a test that still patches the old path (the reason this import exists) runs the real `_shell_group`. Same for every other private name listed here.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/infra/proc.py:14

chunk_findings.detail: `STDLIB_HOMES["subprocess"]` dropped `ddflow.infra.git` and did not name `ddflow.adapters.git`. Git was a subprocess home because that module imports subprocess; this change only relocates it (`ddflow/adapters/git.py` in the manifest). After the move the implementation import is `ddflow.adapters.git`, which is not in the home tuple, so the contract treats a previously allowed owner as a violator. The replacement entry `ddflow.adapters.proc_server` does not cover that import.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:52

chunk_findings.detail: `STDLIB_HOMES["shutil"]` is still `("ddflow.infra.fsio",)` while the fsio home on the line above was moved to `ddflow.adapters.fsio` and `ddflow/infra/fsio.py` is now a re-export shim. Shutil use lives in the moved implementation, not in the shim, so the declared shutil owner no longer imports shutil and the module that does is not a home. Same input that the fsio contract was updated for leaves the shutil contract pointing at the empty shim.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/archdeps.py:54
